clue.text: A small bird of palest hue

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a hen is a female bird, typically a chicken

explanation.surface: A tiny bird is described as having a very pale colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey-white like ash, the palest of complexions.

parts.note: a phrase for being the best in a field, here read literally as the trapeze artists high up under the big top

explanation.surface: A performer has plainly made it in the circus world.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being at the summit of a career, and circus acrobats perform literally high up under the tent roof.

indicators.note: untangling knotted strands rearranges them, so the letters of threads are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone complains that untangling knotted cotton is the toughest job of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disentangling' rearranges the seven letters of THREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardest is the superlative of hard in its sense of tough or demanding, matching most difficult.

parts.note: N is a standard abbreviation for name, as on forms
an auditor is a listener, and the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An accountant's name is mentioned as being close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it is one who hears, hence the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something near is not far off, at a short distance away.

clue.text: It's enough to make bill correspond

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, shortened to ad
to correspond is to match or be equal, which is to equate

explanation.surface: Someone says a payment will suffice to balance the account.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is sufficient, satisfactory in quantity for the need.

clue.text: Chaos caused by woman's dictates about poetry

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana, with the possessive giving DIS

indicators.note: about means the word for dictates goes around the word for poetry

parts.note: dictates are commands, which is to say orders
lines of verse are poetry

explanation.surface: A woman's rules on verse have caused a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the dictates around the poetry; DI is a common crossword woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderliness is a state of untidiness and confusion, the very nature of chaos.

clue.text: Leave opposition leader withdrawing from south American capital

indicators.note: withdrawing from means that letter is taken out of the city name

parts.note: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of opposition

explanation.surface: An opposition leader quits a South American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks O from 'opposition'; 'withdrawing from' removes it from QUITO.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to depart from or abandon, a synonym of leave.

indicators.note: about means the word for dismay wraps around the soldiers

parts.note: to dismay is to horrify, which is to appal
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps often used for soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by what the troops are wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the dismay word around the soldiers; RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword stand-in for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothes, garments worn on the body.

clue.text: Almost topless, yet more than punctual

indicators.note: topless means losing its top letter, in a down clue the first one

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: Someone who is almost bare-chested still turns up ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter N from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means getting there before the set time, going beyond mere punctuality.

clue.text: Interested in a good deal, too

definitions.meaning: read literally, keen on a bargain, focused on a cheap purchase
an idiom meaning as well, in addition

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means additionally, and taken literally it describes someone absorbed in a good buy.

clue.text: Exercise without hesitation in the country

indicators.note: without here is the old sense outside, so the exercise word surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: to exercise is to train, as athletes do
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone does a workout without pausing while out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Reading it as 'remove the hesitation' leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features, which country can mean, as in hilly country.

definitions.meaning: the captain of a ship, or a team's leader

explanation.definitionFit: One who skips is a jumper, and a ship's captain is called both master and this word.

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a Europe-wide accord.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it, so the verb forms match.

indicators.note: in means the old bishop letters go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Wyoming
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An elderly bishop is harassed out in Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the old bishop within the state; RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To worry someone is to bother or pester them, the same as hassle.

parts.note: Fr, short for Father, is the title of a Catholic priest
ay or aye is an old word meaning always or constantly

explanation.surface: A priest keeps stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or fight, a noisy conflict.

clue.text: Philosopher was a cad, tho' good at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the letter for good goes in the middle of the word for a cad

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible man, a cad

explanation.surface: A thinker behaved badly, though deep down he was decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts G in the middle of HEEL. Georg Hegel was a German philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was the German idealist thinker famous for his dialectic.

clue.text: It may be sunk in a marsh afterwards

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something will be lost in a bog later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters within 'marsh afterwards'. Mine shafts are sunk, that is dug downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners sink a vertical passage into the ground to reach coal or ore.

clue.text: Where visiting bell-ringers stand at the start

definitions.meaning: callers who ring a doorbell wait on the doorstep
an idiom for being at the very beginning of something

explanation.definitionFit: Visitors ringing a doorbell wait at the doorway sill, and the phrase also means about to begin.

clue.text: Remain resolved to treat an Irishman

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them
Pat, short for Patrick, is a stereotypical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: Someone stays firm in the decision to buy an Irishman a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pat is to stick to a position and refuse to change, as a poker player keeps a hand.

clue.text: Dash off to render the door more secure

definitions.meaning: to run away or flee quickly

definitions.text: to render the door more secure
definitions.meaning: read literally, fitting a sliding lock to a door

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to flee suddenly, and taken literally it means fitting a door with a lock.

clue.text: French cabinet member with nothing but anger

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
O, the figure zero, means nothing
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A minister in the French government has nothing but fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet member' suggests a minister, but 'cabinet' is furniture and 'member' a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a tall wardrobe or cupboard, the French word for that piece of furniture.

clue.text: Attack and beat small number back

parts.note: a policeman's beat is the round he patrols

indicators.note: back means the short number word is read in reverse

parts.note: No is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone attacks and defeats a small group in return.
explanation.definitionFit: To round on someone is to turn on them suddenly and angrily, a verbal attack.

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor from the Netherlands is accused of being slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in informal use means stupid, slow to understand.

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, as in 'ta, duck', in northern English and Midlands speech

explanation.definitionFit: Waterbirds swim, and in parts of England people address one another as duck, meaning love or dear.

indicators.note: mouthed here means the mouth or opening of the word, its first letter

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling, offensive

explanation.surface: Someone speaks bluntly, swearing and being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul-mouthed' reads as swearing, but it gives the opening letter of 'foul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank speech is candid and direct, as is blunt speech.

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a small stream

explanation.definitionFit: To scorch something is to set fire to it, and in Scotland a stream is called by the same word.

definitions.meaning: a source of water from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A person in good health is fine, and a spring is a source drawn from underground water.

indicators.note: anyway hints that the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone notes that this is how the Queen is addressed, at any rate.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty, the Queen, who is addressed in this way after the first Your Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction of madam, it is the form used when speaking to the Queen.

parts.note: to chime with is to agree with or match
RA, Royal Academician, is a distinguished painter, with the possessive as a link

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with an artist's wonderful notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or impossible fancy, like the mythical beast made of several animals.

clue.text: Show politeness to ladies, but not one's date

definitions.meaning: rise to one's feet when women enter, an old courtesy
fail to turn up for a romantic meeting

explanation.definitionFit: Rising to one's feet is old-fashioned courtesy, and jilting a date by not appearing has the same phrasal verb.
British money is called the pound and also by this name, which also means of excellent character.

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for encountered surrounds the word an

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: Someone met a famous painter but somehow without being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. Édouard Manet was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was the celebrated French painter of Olympia and Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe.
